_readme: FAQ. status 'sample': answers that describe how the shop works are written for the design sample and need the owner's confirmation. Answers can use {{tokens}} from business.json.

items.q: How do I get roadside help?
items.a: Call {{phone}}. Tell us where you are, what the truck is doing and whether you're loaded. You can also use the share-location button on our request page to send your exact spot.

items.q: Do you cover the whole Dallas–Fort Worth area?
items.a: We cover {{serviceArea}}. If you're outside it, call anyway and we'll tell you honestly what we can do.

items.q: What if you can't fix it at the roadside?
items.a: We'll tell you plainly and help arrange a tow to the shop, so you're never left guessing what happens next.

items.q: What should I do before help arrives?
items.a: Turn on your hazard flashers, set out warning devices as required, and stay clear of traffic. Our guide to the first ten minutes of a breakdown walks through it step by step.
Tractors, straight trucks and trailers: brakes and air systems, diesel engines and aftertreatment, electrical, suspension, tires and wheel ends, trailer bodies, inspections and routine maintenance.

items.q: Is there a warranty on repairs?
How often is a DOT annual inspection required?
items.a: At least once every 12 months, under 49 CFR 396.17.

items.q: What does a DOT annual inspection cover?
items.a: At minimum, the components listed in Appendix A to 49 CFR Part 396: the brake system, coupling devices, exhaust, fuel system, lighting, safe loading, steering, suspension, frame, tires, wheels and rims, windshield glazing and wipers, and rear impact guards, among others.

items.q: Can I get an itemized invoice for my records?
items.a: Yes. You'll get a clear, itemized invoice for every job.
